content.jointProblem: Where should Serbian Cyrillic/Latin transliteration and normalization be applied in the KlozuraPro search pipeline — at indexing time, at query time, or both — so that PostgreSQL full-text search returns contract documents for cross-script and mixed-script queries without noticeably increasing response time? The first study would test retrieval effectiveness and latency on representative contract search logs and documents, including ambiguous Latin-to-Cyrillic mappings.

rationale.text: Rajić has direct experience building rule-based normalization layers for non-standard Serbian orthography before downstream language processing.

sources.quote: The paper describes a post-processing layer that applies rule-based normalization to the most frequent respelling patterns before tagging.

rationale.text: He has built a manually curated Serbian lexical resource for mapping orthographic variants to standard forms, relevant to handling script and spelling variability.

sources.quote: manually curated lexicon mapping 8,740 informal orthographic variants of Serbian word forms to their standard dictionary entries

rationale.text: His cross-domain Serbian morpho-syntactic work includes legal short text as a target domain, giving evidence of Serbian legal-text processing experience.

sources.quote: automotive-to-legal transfer retains 91.2% of in-domain F1

rationale.text: He has practical experience coordinating company data-sharing agreements for pseudonymised text, which fits a study requiring access to contract search logs and documents.

sources.quote: coordinated data-sharing agreements with four domestic companies to obtain pseudonymised customer communication text

constraints.text: The solution must handle mixed-script contracts, not only fully-Cyrillic or fully-Latin documents.

sources.quote: robust enough to handle mixed-script documents, not just fully-Cyrillic or fully-Latin ones

constraints.text: Search latency must not increase noticeably.

sources.quote: does not slow down search response times noticeably

constraints.text: The work must address PostgreSQL full-text search treating Cyrillic and Latin as different character sets.

sources.quote: full-text search index in PostgreSQL treats the two scripts as completely different character sets

constraints.text: The plan must account for ambiguous Latin-to-Cyrillic mappings where dialect conventions produce different Cyrillic letters.

sources.quote: same Latin sequence maps to different Cyrillic letters depending on dialect conventions

constraints.text: Company engineering capacity is one backend engineer for at most six weeks.

sources.quote: We have one backend engineer who can work on this for up to six weeks.

constraints.text: The collaboration must separate research outputs from production deployment, because the researcher's group is described as producing corpora, models and reports rather than production-ready applications.

sources.quote: his group produces annotated corpora, trained models, and technical reports rather than production-ready applications

risks: The researcher's documented normalization work concerns informal respelling and orthographic variants, not Cyrillic-Latin transliteration or PostgreSQL full-text search; this transfer gap should be tested in the first experiment.
Cross-domain evidence covers morpho-syntactic tagging on legal advice forum excerpts, not contract search or transliteration, so legal contract language may still behave differently.

The researcher's group is described as producing annotated corpora, trained models and technical reports rather than production-ready applications, while the company needs a deployable search improvement.
The collaboration depends on the company sharing text data for annotation and evaluation, which matches the researcher's stated preference but may be constrained by client confidentiality.
Srđan Rajić's availability is unknown, so scheduling and supervision capacity are unresolved.
The company's one-backend-engineer, six-week capacity may be too short for annotation, evaluation and integration if the first experiment reveals substantial edge cases.
questions: Can Lex Automatika provide representative pseudonymised contract documents and search logs covering Latin, Cyrillic and mixed-script queries for evaluation?
What latency threshold defines 'not noticeably' slower search for the company?
Which Latin-to-Cyrillic mapping conventions and dialect edge cases should be treated as correct for the company's contracts?
Is Srđan Rajić available for this collaboration, and at what capacity? His availability is currently unknown.
Who will implement and maintain the production search change after the research prototype, given the six-week backend engineering limit?
What data governance and pseudonymisation constraints apply to using client contract text in the study?
